h1: Lefroy Brooks installation in Gerrards Cross

hero.intro: Homeowners in Gerrards Cross who choose Lefroy Brooks are usually after one thing: a bathroom that looks like the plumbing has always been there, built using cross-head handles, exposed pipe runs and period-inspired profiles instead of the concealed, minimal brassware fitted as standard in most new bathrooms. Gerrards Cross is an affluent Buckinghamshire commuter village close to Beaconsfield and Chalfont St Peter, around 25 to 30 minutes by road from our Bracknell base — close enough that a Lefroy Brooks installation here runs on the same fit-only model as the rest of our coverage area. This page covers what the brand is known for, what we install from it, what that means for a Gerrards Cross property, and how booking a survey works.

sections.heading: What Lefroy Brooks is known for
sections.body: Lefroy Brooks is built around period-inspired profiles, cross-head handles and exposed pipe runs — brassware and sanitaryware designed to be seen rather than concealed behind a panel or chased into a wall. That's the opposite approach to most contemporary brands, which hide the plumbing and leave only a tap head or shower control visible. With Lefroy Brooks, every bracket, joint and length of pipe is part of the finished look, which means it has to be set out and finished to that standard from the first fix onward.

sections.heading: What we install from the Lefroy Brooks range
sections.body: We fit the taps, shower valves and sanitaryware you choose from the Lefroy Brooks range, as part of a fit-only service: you buy the products, we provide the strip-out, first fix, plumbing, tiling and snagging to install them. The exposed-pipework style means the first-fix stage is more exacting than a standard concealed valve installation — the pipe runs and bracket positions are set out before any tiling goes on, because there's no panel to hide a compromise behind later.
